item.title: Oil Holds Drop as Saudi Arabian Price Cut Amplifies Glut Concern
item.description: Oil held a drop on signs of growing global oversupply, with Saudi Arabia slashing prices of its main grade to Asia and maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz picking up.

item.title: Japan Drives Asia Offshore Bonds to Record, Surpassing China Era
item.description: Japanese borrowers drove quarterly issuance in Asia Pacific’s offshore bond market to a record, eclipsing the previous peak set during an era of Chinese corporate dominance.

item.title: Rivian Offers 75 Million Shares to Meet US Energy Loan Terms
item.description: Rivian Automotive Inc. is offering to sell 75 million shares as the electric vehicle company seeks to fund equity contributions related to a US Department of Energy loan.

item.title: 【今朝の5本】仕事を始める前に読んでおきたい厳選ニュース
item.description: 世界トップ5目指すとMUFG社長、SKハイニックス米上場へ、米株見通し、サウジ原油値下げ、ホルムズ脱出へ

item.title: KKR’s Private Credit Clients Slow Down Their Redemption Requests
item.description: Investors in a KKR & Co. retail private credit fund got back all of their requested cash in the second quarter, a sign that individual investors’ skittishness over the asset class may be easing.

item.title: Traders Are Most Positive on Dollar Since 2015 as Fed Hike Looms
item.description: Global traders have turned the most positive on the outlook for the dollar since 2015 as bets that borrowing costs will remain elevated for longer have fueled a monthlong rally in the US currency.

item.title: Tether’s Former CIO Plans Sale of Stake in Stablecoin Giant
item.description: Richard Heathcote, who until earlier this year oversaw stablecoin giant Tether Holdings SA’s investment portfolio, is planning to sell a small stake in the company, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Hedge Funds Turn Most Negative on the Japanese Yen Since 2007
item.description: Hedge funds turned the most negative on the yen since 2007 as the currency trades near its weakest level in four decades.

item.title: Hertz Bears Boost Short Bets to Record After Shares Plummet 60%
item.description: Short sellers are anticipating more pain ahead for Hertz Global Holdings Inc. after the stock sank nearly 60% in less than two weeks.

item.title: Lone Pine Gains 43% in First Half on Both Long and Short Bets
item.description: Lone Pine Capital posted a 43% gain for its hedge fund investors through June, notching one of its best-ever starts to a year and landing it among 2026’s top performers.

item.title: Distressed Funds Explore Swap of Strategy Holdings Amid Rout
item.description: Distressed-debt funds that snapped up Strategy Inc.’s beaten-down preferred shares are in talks with one of the company’s bankers about swapping them for other securities, pitching it as a win-win as the relentless rout in crypto puts the Bitcoin accumulator in an increasingly tough spot.

item.title: New Zealand Set to Raise Key Rate, Decision Less of a Slam Dunk
item.description: New Zealand’s central bank is poised to raise its key interest rate this week, most economists and traders reckon, beginning a gradual unwinding of stimulus as it aims to head off emerging inflationary pressures.

item.title: Advertising Technology Firm Criteo Attracts Vista Equity-Backed Takeover Offer
item.description: Vista Equity Partners and the investment firm Quinti Capital have teamed up on a takeover offer for French advertising-technology company Criteo SA, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Public Spending in Mexico Ends Prolonged Fall in Fixed Investment
item.description: A key measure of investments in Mexico snapped back in April driven largely by government spending while private investment lagged, offering scant relief to President Claudia Sheinbaum’s push for stronger economic growth.

item.title: Trump Bitcoin Reserve Faces Hurdles as Departments Seek Control
item.description: The Trump administration’s plan to create a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve has been complicated by two government departments vying to run it, alongside questions about which has the legal authority to do so.

item.title: Economies Thrive With Older, Smaller Population, New Study Finds
item.description: Declining birth rates around the world have gotten many people worried about the economic impact, with predictions of slower growth and less innovation. But a new paper finds that the opposite may be true.

item.title: Ardian’s Santé Cie Seeks to Enter French Restructuring Procedure
item.description: Santé Cie SAS is seeking to enter French restructuring proceedings after some of its cash assets were seized as part of an investigation from the authorities into alleged corruption and money laundering.

item.title: Sports-Related Deals on the Rise, Says William Blair’s IB Head
item.description: Acquisitions in the sports industry are set to increase as investors leverage a slew of different approaches to the fast-growing sector, according to William Blair & Co.’s head of investment banking.

item.title: Tepper’s Appaloosa Soars 32% in First Half on Memory-Chip Makers
item.description: David Tepper’s Appaloosa Management returned 32% in the first half of the year, fueled by bets on the high-flying memory-chip sector.

item.title: Dental Chain Owner Aspen Drops WellNow Sale as Lenders Lawyer Up
item.description: The Aspen Group has indicated it’s no longer moving ahead with a planned sale of its urgent care clinic chain WellNow, after seeking buyers amid an effort to address a looming debt deadline that’s also prompted its lenders to retain lawyers.

item.title: The Restaurant Economy Doesn’t Look K-Shaped
item.description: It looks like a broad based boom.

item.title: Boston Airport Borrows $812 Million for Revamp as Traffic Soars
item.description: The busiest airport in New England is tapping the municipal bond market to remodel its facilities and keep up with passenger growth.

item.title: WEF Founder Schwab Claims He Found Spying Device at His Home
item.description: World Economic Forum founder Klaus Schwab has filed a criminal complaint following the alleged discovery of a secret listening device planted in his home office in Geneva.

item.title: Trans Mountain 3.0 Revives Indigenous Pipeline Ownership Push
item.description: Canada’s announcement last week that Trans Mountain Corp. will build a 1 million-barrel-a-day oil pipeline along the government-owned company’s existing Alberta-to-British Columbia route is rekindling Indigenous interest in acquiring a stake in the company.

item.title: Argentina Shuns Markets for Now, Sees Investment Grade by 2031
item.description: President Javier Milei’s administration is targeting investment-grade status for Argentina by the end of a potential second term in 2031, while continuing to shun international debt markets.

item.title: Hedge Fund Veterans Are Accelerating a Major Shift in Development Finance
item.description: A group of hedge fund veterans is helping drive a fundamental shift in how to generate financing for developing nations.

item.title: Germany to Sweeten Terms of Gas Plant Auction to Draw More Bids
item.description: Germany will lift the maximum amount it will pay developers in upcoming auctions for gas-fired power plants as it seeks to attract more bids for urgently needed back-up power capacity.

item.title: Bank of Canada Surveys Show War Boosted Inflation Expectations, Investment
item.description: The war in Iran caused a spike in Canadian inflation expectations and is leading the country’s oil producers to boost their investment and production plans.

item.title: Peace Deal Doesn’t Restore Pre-War Situation, ECB’s Schnabel Says
item.description: Peace efforts in the Middle East have helped bring energy prices down rapidly but haven’t restored the position the world was in before hostilities erupted, according to European Central Bank Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel.

item.title: Ontario, Alberta Pitch Cross-Canada Oil Pipeline to Ease US Reliance
item.description: Alberta and Ontario proposed a crude oil pipeline and energy corridor across Canada as a way of reducing the country’s dependence on the US.
